tuning_targets: share of parseable final lines at least 0.97 for every style, abstain style abstaining on roughly 0.15 to 0.45 of the tuning questions. Accuracy is recorded and was not a target. No judge call was made during tuning.
selection_note: Wordings were compared only on the share of parseable final lines and on how often the abstain style abstains. The assert and hedge wordings are those of v3 (unchanged in every later version). Instructions that only ask the model to abstain when unsure (v1 to v4, v6) gave 0.00 to 0.07 abstention. Making "I don't know" the default reply moved it: 0.69 with "complete certainty" (v5a), 0.22 with "confidence" (v7c), 0.23 with an added sentence that most questions can be answered (v7d). v7c and v7d both meet the two targets on all 100 rows and are tied on them. v7c was taken because its criterion word is the one in the plan (abstain if not confident) and it makes no statement about how much the model knows. Accuracy was printed next to the targets during tuning and was not used. On the tuning rows v7c also has the higher accuracy when answering (0.85 against 0.81 for v7d), which the choice did not rely on. The abstention rate is very sensitive to the wording of the reply-shape paragraph (v8: 0.02 to 0.09 with the same head), so the rate on other questions may differ from the tuning rate. The hedge style opens with "I am fairly sure" or "I'm fairly sure" in most replies, so it marks a register and is not a calibrated confidence.
